In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of numeric methods to support the design of human-machine systems.
the use of numeric methods to evaluate the impact on a design that is based on a scenario based analysis.
how numeric methods can help in the design phase, where the focus is on the early identification of requirements and how they can be prioritised.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the application of a numeric method to support the design of systems is a useful tool.
scenario-based design methods can be used as a means to identify new requirements, but the impact of these requirements on the overall system design is best assessed using numeric methods.
numeric and descriptive methods are not mutually exclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of descriptive and numeric methods is a promising approach for the analysis of human reliability.
numeric methods can be useful in the evaluation of consequences of scenarios identified by descriptive methods.
the combination of scenario analysis and numeric analysis can provide a better basis for the refinement of a design than either of these techniques in isolation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
numeric methods can be useful for evaluating the consequences of new requirements.
scenario based design should include numeric analysis of the impact of requirements.
a combination of descriptive and numeric methods is required to fully understand the implications of a design.
